title: May motorbike ka sa Japan? Puwede ka nang pumili ng plate number from October 19
summary: Japan will open its first motorcycle choice-number system on October 19, 2026. Eligible motorcycles over 125cc can apply online or at a counter, with plate fees generally ¥2,500–¥3,000 per plate. Popular numbers use a lottery.
why_it_matters: Motorcycle owners who want a meaningful or easy-to-remember four-digit number now have a concrete application date, price range and eligibility rules. Riders with 125cc-or-less motorcycles should not apply because municipal plates are outside this national system.

claims.text: Applications for Japan's motorcycle choice-number system start on October 19, 2026, and can be made online or at a counter.
The system covers eligible light motorcycles over 125cc through 250cc and small motorcycles over 250cc; motorcycles of 125cc or less are excluded because their plates are issued by municipalities.
Business-use and rental motorcycles are excluded, and trailers are also excluded from the light-motorcycle category.

Applicants choose the four Arabic digits displayed on the motorcycle plate. National lottery numbers are 1, 7, 8, 88, 333, 358, 555, 777, 888, 1111 and 8888; additional regional lottery numbers may apply.
The published application fee is ¥2,500–¥3,000 per plate including tax, with the exact amount depending on the applicable plate area.

Owners targeting a lottery number should prepare before October 19 rather than assuming an early application guarantees that number, because the listed popular numbers are allocated by weekly computerized lottery.
claims.basis: Inference from MLIT's weekly lottery rule

content.key_message: Kung eligible motorcycle mo ay over 125cc at gusto mo ng specific four-digit plate number, applications open October 19. Check first kung covered ang bike at kung lottery number ang gusto mo.
content.who_is_affected: Owners of eligible light motorcycles over 125cc through 250cc and small motorcycles over 250cc in Japan who want to choose the four-digit number on their plate.
content.financial_impact: MLIT lists ¥2,500–¥3,000 per plate including tax. Check the exact local amount before paying.
content.risk_if_ignored: Main risk is wasted preparation or payment assumptions: 125cc-or-less municipal plates, business-use and rental motorcycles are outside this system, and popular numbers are not guaranteed because they use a lottery.
content.deadline: No general closing deadline is announced. October 19, 2026 is the application start date.
content.effort: Low to medium: confirm motorcycle category, decide the four digits, check whether they are lottery-controlled, then apply online or through the relevant counter route.
content.potential_benefit: Lets an eligible motorcycle owner request a memorable or personally meaningful four-digit plate number under the new national system.
content.downside: There is an application/plate cost and lottery-controlled numbers are not guaranteed.
content.what_would_change_mind: A later MLIT notice changing the October 19 start date, eligibility, lottery-number list, application route or published fees.
what_to_do_now: Check the bike's displacement and use category. 125cc or less is not covered.
Choose the four Arabic digits you want on the plate.
Check whether your number is on the national or regional lottery list.
From October 19, use the official online application route or the relevant counter; MLIT also says a motorcycle shop, repair shop or administrative scrivener can be consulted.
Keep the application/receipt or reservation evidence until the plate process is complete.
prepare: Motorcycle registration/details needed by the official application process
Preferred four-digit number plus a backup plan if the number is lottery-controlled
¥2,500–¥3,000 per plate based on the published range; confirm the exact local fee
avoid: Do not assume applying first guarantees a popular lottery number.
Do not rely on unofficial sellers for eligibility or fee claims when the MLIT guidance is available.
content.watch: Check MLIT and the official choice-number application site for regional lottery numbers and exact local plate fees before submitting.
content.bottom_line: FACT: Japan's motorcycle choice-number applications start October 19 for eligible motorcycles over 125cc, with a published ¥2,500–¥3,000-per-plate range and lotteries for popular numbers. INFERENCE: riders who care about a specific popular number should prepare now, but there is no evidence that filing earlier guarantees a lottery-controlled number.
